newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bank of Osaka to write off Y30 bln problem loans.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Osaka to write off Y30 bln problem loans.

text.p: Bank of Osaka Ltd said on Friday that it would write off about 30 billion yen worth of problem loans in the year to March 31, 1997, but added that it would maintain its current profit forecast for the 1996/97 year.
The regional bank said in a statement it has maintained its parent current profit forecast of about two billion yen and net profit forecast of about one billion yen in 1996/97.
It said it would speed up write-offs of its problem loans and support to its affiliate in a bid to complete its programme to deal with problem loans a year earlier than originally planned.
The bank aims to resume dividend payments after 1997/98 as soon as possible, the statement said.
The bank's capital adequacy ratio is expected to rise to about 4.6 percent by the end of March 1997, up about 0.4 percentage point from the end of September 1996, it said.

Japan is scheduled to introduce formal capital adequacy standards in April 1998 under which banks operating only in Japan must have a capital adequacy ratio of at least four percent to be considered "adequately capitalised".
